provenance.paper_title: eMEM: A Hybrid Spatio-Temporal Memory System For Embodied Agents

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: SQLite, HNSW, and R-tree indexes expose meaning-, time-, and space-aware recall over one graph.

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: A tiered pipeline transforms raw observations into compressed summaries for cross-layer recall.
Tiered consolidation compresses raw perceptual observations into summaries. For eMEM, this specifically supports episodic or hierarchical summarization of multi-index spatiotemporal graph.
Observations move through multiple consolidation layers under a fixed pipeline. For eMEM, this specifically supports migration between memory tiers of multi-index spatiotemporal graph.

Consolidation reduces redundant observations while preserving cross-layer links. For eMEM, this specifically supports merging or deduplication of overlapping entries of multi-index spatiotemporal graph.
During operation, eMEM applies progressive decay of stored importance or retention to multi-index spatiotemporal graph; the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 3): During inference, the operative memory component (multi-index spatiotemporal graph) changes through episodic or hierarchical summarization, migration between memory tiers, merging or deduplication of overlapping entries, progressive decay of stored importance or retention; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
